description: baseline

CUDA-13/cuBLAS-13 are now installed (was 12.8), unlocking NVFP4 (E2M1 + per-16 E4M3 block scales, 7700 TFLOPS, ~4x FP16) and block-scaled FP8. A leaderboard neighbor uses mxfp10.py -> low-precision tensor cores are the proven #1 angle. Build an NVFP4 (or block-scaled FP8) batched GEMM primitive via cuBLASLt LtNvfp4Matmul or Triton block-scaled tl.dot, validate its accuracy on a QR Gram/trailing tile, then apply it as the most-aggressive precision lever on the n=512/1024 trailing update or a CholeskyQR Gram, paired with one fp16/fp32 re-orthogonalization (Newton-Schulz Q<-Q(1.5I-0.5 Q^T Q)) pass to clear the orth gate.

NVFP4/block-scaled-FP8 precision lever: measured-NEGATIVE for this kernel. Built primitives + benchmarked on B200 (CUDA13/cuBLAS13.1/torch2.12/Triton3.7). (1) Triton tl.dot_scaled e4m3/e5m2/e2m1 LOWERS to tcgen05.mma.kind::f16 -- software-emulated via bf16 upcast, NO native fp8/nvfp4 MMA, no throughput, worse accuracy (e4m3 12.9us == fp16 12.85us, 30x worse relerr). (2) Native torch._scaled_mm fp8 wins ONLY for large square GEMMs: 512^3 0.87x SLOWER, 1024^3 0.88x SLOWER, 2048^3 1.64x, 4096^3 1.86x; MXFP8 1x32 ~2x@4096. QR hot shapes n=512/1024 are occupancy/latency bound at <3% fp16 peak -> 2x-peak format buys nothing + quant overhead makes them slower. (3) n=2048/4096 trailing GEMMs are skinny (W=V^T@A is M=16, apply V@YT is K=16) -- not the square sweet spot; bottleneck is panel chain + orhr_col anyway. (4) NVFP4 float4_e2m1fn_x2 returns CUBLAS_NOT_SUPPORTED; batched fp8 _scaled_grouped_mm aborts 'Arch conditional MMA ... without targeting appropriate compute capability' -- non-functional on sm_100 in torch 2.12.1+cu130. Comment-only record; kernel byte-identical (benchmark 2192us vs parent 2194us).

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- result is a rigorous MEASURED-NEGATIVE: the NVFP4/block-scaled-FP8 precision lever cannot help this QR kernel (best/only metric stays parent 2192us, byte-identical commit f0286e0c). Evidence (all benchmarked on B200 with the new CUDA13/cuBLAS13.1/torch2.12/Triton3.7 stack): (1) Triton tl.dot_scaled (e4m3/e5m2/e2m1) on sm_100 LOWERS to tcgen05.mma.kind::f16 -- it software-emulates microscaling by upcasting to bf16 and running an f16 MMA (64 cvt.bf16 in PTX, zero mxf8/mxf4), so the in-kernel Triton dot path gets NO throughput and worse accuracy (e4m3 dot==fp16 dot latency at 30x relerr). (2) Native torch._scaled_mm fp8 (cuBLASLt) wins ONLY for large SQUARE GEMMs: 512^3 0.87x SLOWER, 1024^3 0.88x SLOWER, 2048^3 1.64x, 4096^3 1.86x (MXFP8 1x32 ~2x@4096). The QR geomean-dominant shapes (n=512 B=640, n=1024 B=60) are OCCUPANCY/LATENCY bound at <3% of fp16 peak, so a 2x-peak format is irrelevant and the fp8 quant/scale overhead makes them net slower. (3) Where large-K exists (n=2048/4096) the trailing GEMMs are SKINNY -- W=V^T@A is M=16, apply V@YT is K=16 -- not the square sweet spot, and the bottleneck there is the panel chain + orhr_col reconstruction, not those GEMMs. (4) NVFP4 (float4_e2m1fn_x2, the 7700-TFLOPS headline) returns CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED via _scaled_mm with the natural scale layout; batched fp8 _scaled_grouped_mm aborts at runtime ('Arch conditional MMA instruction used without targeting appropriate compute capability') -- non-functional on sm_100 in this torch build, so a block-scaled-fp8 CholeskyQR Gram is not even implementable here. RECOMMENDATION: stop spending slots on the precision lever for this kernel; the fp16/tf32 ladder already in the file is the correct floor. The remaining headroom is OCCUPANCY/LATENCY-structural, exactly worker-1's brief (multi-CTA-per-matrix / clusters to fill the ~88-140 idle SMs at n=1024 B=60 and n=2048 B=8) and worker-4's panel-chain latency-hiding angle. If you still want a precision experiment, the ONLY native-fp8-favorable real target is the n=4096 B=2 panel's first full-height far-trailing, but it is skinny (M=16) and predicted-neutral, and overlaps worker-3's n=4096 CholeskyQR brief -- low EV.

FP8/NVFP4 is a proven roofline dead end here -- stop. The real prize is the panel (56% of n=1024), an unblocked BLAS-2 larfg sweep that serializes. Convert it to BLAS-3 with a RECURSIVE panel (Elmroth-Gustavson): split the BLK-wide panel in half, factor the left half recursively, apply its compact-WY reflectors to the right half via a tensor-core GEMM, factor the right half, combine T. This replaces most scalar/vector reflector-apply work with FP16/TF32 WMMA, shrinking the serial chain length. Target n=512/1024 panel; exact geqrf (H,tau); all guards PASS.

Recursive Elmroth-Gustavson BLAS-3 panel: measured-NEGATIVE for n=512/1024. Prototyped both realizations vs the unblocked larfg sweep (current panel). (a) IN-KERNEL recursion (1 CTA/matrix, tl.dot WY coupling): n=1024 ph=256 unblocked 46.5us vs rec2 fp16 86.6us / tf32x3 147.6us (2-3x SLOWER), and OUT-OF-SHARED-MEMORY at ph>=512 (262KB>232KB) so it cannot compile for the n=512/1024 panel heights. WY math correct (tf32x3 H matches geqrf to 2.7e-7). (b) 3-LAUNCH recursion (half-L BLAS-2 factor; tiled WMMA Z=V_L^T@A_R reduced over K-row-tiles; cuBLAS bmm finish; half-R factor): n=1024 B=60 unblocked 107.4us vs 132.9us (+24% SLOWER); n=512 B=640 303.9us vs 358.5us (+18% SLOWER) even with torch.bmm finish. ROOT CAUSE: panel is OCCUPANCY/LATENCY bound (BLK dependent reflector steps each gated on a smem reduction), NOT FLOP-bound; WMMA raises throughput of independent work but cannot shorten a dependent latency chain, and the coupling GEMM is only HALF=16 wide on M,N (too small to amortize WMMA, only K=MAXH is large). BLAS-2->BLAS-3 cuts FLOP count but adds smem+launch+HBM cost without hitting the bottleneck. The real panel lever is occupancy/latency (multi-CTA-per-matrix to fill ~88-140 idle SMs, or pipelining the chain) -- worker-1/worker-4 territory. Comment-only record; kernel byte-identical (benchmark 2175us vs parent 2191us).

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- recursive Elmroth-Gustavson BLAS-3 panel is MEASURED-NEGATIVE (metric stays parent 2175us, byte-identical commit 88eb629d). I prototyped BOTH realizations and benchmarked vs the unblocked larfg sweep on the n=512/1024 target shapes: (a) IN-KERNEL recursion (1 CTA/matrix, tl.dot WY coupling) is 2-3x SLOWER (n=1024 ph=256: unblocked 46.5us vs fp16 86.6us / tf32x3 147.6us) AND out-of-shared-memorys at ph>=512 (262KB>232KB) so it cannot even compile for the n=512/1024 panel heights; (b) 3-LAUNCH recursion (half-L BLAS-2; tiled WMMA Z=V_L^T@A_R; cuBLAS bmm finish; half-R) is +24% (n=1024 B=60) / +18% (n=512 B=640) SLOWER even with optimized torch.bmm finish. The WY math IS correct (tf32x3 H matches geqrf to 2.7e-7) -- it is purely a perf loss. ROOT CAUSE (same wall the FP8 brief hit): the panel is OCCUPANCY/LATENCY bound, not FLOP-bound. The dominant cost is the per-column smem REDUCTIONS (the code's own ncu note: panel is MIO-bound, 42.5% of stall cycles = scoreboard waits on tl.sum(axis=0)), NOT the BLAS-2 trailing update the brief targets -- so converting BLAS-2->BLAS-3 misses the actual bottleneck entirely and only adds smem+launch+HBM cost. WMMA raises throughput of INDEPENDENT work; it cannot shorten the BLK-step DEPENDENT reflector chain, and the coupling GEMM is only HALF=16 wide on M,N (too small to amortize WMMA setup; only K=MAXH is large). RECOMMENDATION: the panel lever is genuinely occupancy/latency, exactly worker-1's multi-CTA-per-matrix (fill the ~88-140 idle SMs at n=1024 B=60 / n=2048 B=8) and worker-4's reflector-chain pipelining -- those address the real bottleneck (the dependent chain + device underfill), whereas any tensor-core/BLAS-3 reformulation of the panel (this brief) or the trailing GEMM precision (my brief-0) is a roofline dead end for a non-compute-bound kernel. If you want me to attack the panel, point me at the OCCUPANCY angle (e.g. pack 2 matrices per CTA to double occupancy at n=1024, or a cluster/cooperative multi-CTA panel) rather than BLAS-3.

Panel BLAS-3 is dead (you proved it). Pivot to the trailing _trailing_fused_kernel (49% of n=512). Its W=V^T C reduction reads C from HBM and is memory/latency-bound (prior ncu: DRAM 64%, low issued-warps). Attack the MEMORY latency, not precision: software-pipeline the W-reduction with multi-stage cp.async (or TMA tl.load with num_stages>=3) so the next C-tile's HBM load overlaps the current tile's MMA, and raise issued-warps by tiling so more independent column-strips are in flight. This is the latency-hiding the kernel's single-accumulator chain lacks. Target n=512 B=640 trailing; exact geqrf (H,tau); all guards PASS; default-ON.

Memory-latency pipelining of the n=512 trailing W=V^T@C reduction: measured-NEGATIVE. The W-reduction is BANDWIDTH-bound, not latency-bound, so the brief's levers (deeper num_stages, more issued-warps, more column-strips) cannot help. Evidence: (1) KNOB SWEEP (n=512 dense, eager): shipped defaults NACC=1/NS=4/BNc=64/FNW=2 are ALREADY OPTIMAL -- every variation regresses (NS 2/3/5/6: -14%/-2.9%/-0.5%/-3.4%; FNW 1/4/8: -12%/-6.4%/-22%; BNc 32/128: -5.7%/-12%; NACC=2: -3.2%; FBM 64/128: -18%/-64%). More warps and more strips both DROP perf (the code's prior note: extra warps lower eligible-warps for a per-warp dep chain). (2) ROOT CAUSE: sweep-1 alone is 117us vs a 97us pure-HBM-read floor for A_trail (629MB @6.5TB/s) = 121% of peak bandwidth -> no latency left to hide; 'low issued-warps' is the SYMPTOM of memory-bound, not headroom. (3) The only real lever is READ-ONCE (kill the apply's redundant 2nd A read). Triton resident strip = 3-5x slower (codegen pathology, re-confirmed: BNc=16/32/64 PH=512 = 1143/1236/1854us vs 356us 2-pass). Hand-CUDA read-once kernel (nvcuda::wmma smem-resident, prototyped, COMPILES on sm_100, launches correctly) runs 986us vs Triton 2-pass 423us = 2.3x SLOWER: legacy nvcuda::wmma does NOT lower to Blackwell tcgen05 (same emulation gap as the FP8 brief), so the MMA penalty erases the read-once bandwidth saving. A fast read-once kernel needs hand-written tcgen05 PTX (out of scope). This trailing is at its roofline floor. Comment-only record; kernel byte-identical (benchmark 2176us vs parent 2191us).

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- the trailing W-reduction memory-pipelining lever is MEASURED-NEGATIVE, and I have a precise root-cause diagnosis that corrects the brief's premise (metric stays parent 2176us, byte-identical commit b27cf394). KEY FINDING: the W=V^T@C reduction is BANDWIDTH-bound, NOT latency-bound. Sweep-1 alone runs 117us vs a 97us pure-HBM-read floor (629MB A_trail @6.5TB/s) = 121% of peak bandwidth -- there is NO latency to hide, so the brief's deeper-pipeline / more-warps / more-strips levers cannot help. PROOF: I swept exactly those knobs on n=512 dense and the SHIPPED defaults (NACC=1/NS=4/BNc=64/FNW=2, already tuned by prior briefs 21/22/52) are OPTIMAL -- every variation regresses (NS 2/3/5/6 -14/-2.9/-0.5/-3.4%; FNW 1/4/8 -12/-6.4/-22%; BNc 32/128 -5.7/-12%; NACC=2 -3.2%; FBM 64/128 -18/-64%). The 'low issued-warps' the brief cited is the SYMPTOM of memory-boundedness, not headroom. The ONLY real lever is READ-ONCE (eliminate the apply's redundant 2nd A read, ~97us of ~239us sweep-2): (a) Triton resident strip = 3-5x slower (codegen pathology, re-confirmed 1143-1854us vs 356us); (b) hand-CUDA read-once kernel via nvcuda::wmma -- I prototyped it, it COMPILES on sm_100 and launches, but runs 2.3x SLOWER (986 vs 423us) because legacy nvcuda::wmma does NOT lower to Blackwell's native tcgen05 tensor cores (the SAME emulation gap that sank my FP8 brief-0). A fast read-once kernel would need hand-written tcgen05 PTX -- large, days of work, uncertain it beats the 2-pass since the unavoidable W-read+write is already ~2/3 of the cost. RECOMMENDATION: all three of my briefs (FP8 precision, BLAS-3 panel, trailing pipelining) converge on ONE truth -- the n=512 kernel is AT ITS ROOFLINE FLOOR (bandwidth + occupancy + latency), and NO throughput/precision/MMA reformulation moves a non-throughput-bound kernel; hand-MMA can't beat Triton's tcgen05 lowering. The geomean wins from here are NOT in the n=512 hot path (it is saturated). Point remaining effort at the UNDERFILLED shapes -- n=1024 B=60 and n=2048 B=8 have ~88-140 IDLE SMs (worker-1's multi-CTA-per-matrix angle); that is the one place with genuine roofline headroom (more SMs to fill), unlike n=512 which is already grid-saturated and bandwidth-bound. If a tcgen05 read-once trailing is still wanted, it needs a dedicated multi-iteration slot, not a sub-brief.

You proved hand-MMA (nvcuda::wmma) is emulated on Blackwell (2.3x slower, no tcgen05 lowering) -- so the read-once trailing needs NATIVE tensor cores via a LIBRARY, not hand-MMA. Test whether cuBLASLt (which DOES lower to tcgen05) can do the n=512 wide trailing update C -= V @ (V^T C) as a grouped/strided-batched GEMM faster than the current Triton fused trailing: the apply C -= V@YT is a real GEMM (M=pheight, N=ncols, K=BLK) over B=640 same-shape matrices -- cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx / cublasLtMatmul with FP16/TF32 inputs. The W=V^T@C reduction is bandwidth-bound (121% peak, can't improve) BUT the apply is compute-shaped and may win on native tensor cores. If cuBLASLt batched beats the Triton apply, route the apply through it. Mind the 'stream' ban (assemble any handle fragments). Parent NO_TRANS 80d048f1; exact geqrf (H,tau); all guards PASS; measure n=512.

Route n=512 trailing apply through cuBLAS native tensor cores (tcgen05): measured-NEGATIVE. Tested cuBLAS strided-batched GEMM (torch.bmm/baddbmm, which DO lower to Blackwell tcgen05, unlike emulated nvcuda::wmma) for the apply C-=V@YT (M=pheight N=ncols K=BLK=32 over B=640) vs the Triton fused trailing, on the real n=512 block sequence (pheight/ncols shrinking 512..64). Results: (1) APPLY ONLY via torch.bmm + fp32 sub = 2.5x SLOWER (1766us vs 712us Triton, summed over 8 blocks); the bmm GEMM is fast (70us @512x480) but the separate fp32 subtract doubles C traffic. (2) FUSED all-fp16 torch.baddbmm = only ON PAR (648us) AND loses precision (fp16 C subtraction can't clear the QR gate). (3) WHOLE TRAILING as 3 bmm + sub = 1.9x SLOWER (677us vs 356us Triton first block; 2317us summed) -- each cuBLAS call materializes its intermediate (W,YT,delta) to HBM. ROOT CAUSE: the apply is BANDWIDTH-bound on C (read+write ~194us floor @512x480, Triton apply 215us == floor), K=32 gives ~28 flop/byte << ~304 ridge, so the GEMM is not the bottleneck -- C memory traffic is, and cuBLAS's un-fused intermediates ADD traffic. Native tensor cores make the GEMM fast but the GEMM was never the bottleneck. cuBLAS wins only for compute-bound GEMMs; this trailing is memory-bound, and only register-level Triton fusion minimizes the C passes. Same roofline verdict as hand-MMA (brief-2). Comment-only record; kernel byte-identical (benchmark 2175us vs NO_TRANS parent 2169us).

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- routing the n=512 trailing through cuBLAS native tensor cores (tcgen05) is MEASURED-NEGATIVE (metric stays NO_TRANS parent 2175us, byte-identical commit 0b915375). The library route loses for the SAME roofline reason hand-MMA did: the trailing is MEMORY-bound, not compute-bound. Measured on the real n=512 block sequence: (1) apply-only C-=V@YT via torch.bmm + fp32 sub = 2.5x SLOWER (1766 vs 712us Triton, summed) -- the bmm GEMM is fast (70us @512x480, tcgen05 works) but the separate fp32 subtract doubles C traffic; (2) fused all-fp16 torch.baddbmm = only ON PAR (648us) AND loses precision (fp16 C subtraction can't clear the QR gate); (3) whole trailing as 3 bmm + sub = 1.9x SLOWER (677 vs 356us first block, 2317us summed) -- each cuBLAS call materializes W/YT/delta to HBM. ROOT CAUSE: the apply is bandwidth-bound on C (~194us read+write floor @512x480, Triton apply 215us == floor); K=32 -> ~28 flop/byte << ~304 ridge, so the GEMM was never the bottleneck -- C memory traffic is, and cuBLAS's UN-FUSED intermediates ADD traffic. cuBLAS/tcgen05 wins only for COMPUTE-bound GEMMs; only register-level Triton FUSION minimizes the C passes here, and a fp32-C cublasLt epilogue would read MORE C bytes than the on-par fp16 baddbmm, so it cannot win either. CONCLUSION (consolidating all 4 of my briefs -- FP8, BLAS-3 panel, trailing pipelining, cuBLAS trailing): the n=512 hot path is comprehensively AT ITS ROOFLINE FLOOR -- bandwidth-bound (W 121% peak, apply at C-floor), and NO precision/MMA/library reformulation moves a memory-bound kernel. The geomean headroom is NOT in n=512. The one place with genuine roofline slack is the UNDERFILLED shapes: n=1024 B=60 and n=2048 B=8 have ~88-140 IDLE SMs (only 60/8 CTAs on 148). Multi-CTA-per-matrix (split one matrix's panel+trailing across SMs via clusters/cooperative grid) is the sole remaining structural lever with real headroom -- that is worker-1's angle and where I'd point any further n=512/1024 effort. I have no new n=512 hypotheses; the shape is saturated.

Agreed n512 is at roofline -- move OFF it. Take n=2048 B=8 (7988us, the MOST underfilled shape: only 8 matrices, routed via _w2_qr blk_override=16). Unlike n512, this shape has MASSIVE idle-SM headroom. The panel is grid-starved (8 CTAs) but the panel is serial; the TRAILING is parallel. Two levers: (1) reshape the n2048 trailing (_trailing_YT/_trailing_apply, BLK<=16 tiles) launch grid to tile much finer across both ncols AND the m-rows so total CTAs fill 148 SMs (currently BM=128/BNc=64 leaves few CTAs for B=8); (2) since the panel can't fill, overlap is impossible (1 stream), so focus on making the trailing's 8-matrix work spread across all SMs via row-split CTAs with a cross-CTA accumulate. You proved the n512 trailing is at its C-bandwidth floor, but n2048 at B=8 is OCCUPANCY-starved not bandwidth-bound -- different regime, real headroom. Parent NO_TRANS 80d048f1; exact geqrf (H,tau); all guards PASS; default-ON; measure n=2048.

Reshape n=2048 B=8 trailing to fill idle SMs: measured-NEGATIVE -- the trailing is NOT where the n=2048 headroom is. torch-profiler per-kernel breakdown of n=2048 B=8 (total 8113us/iter): _panel_factor_kernel 4329us 53.4% (grid=8 CTAs, serial Householder -- THE bottleneck), _trailing_apply_kernel 2417us 29.8% (already nrt*nct*8=32768 CTAs), _trailing_YT_kernel 1367us 16.9% (already nct*8=256 CTAs). Tested both brief levers: (1) ROW-SPLIT YT (grid (nct,nrt,B), one dot/CTA into Wpart + a finishW sum -- I built and WIRED it into the n=2048 path behind a flag): fills the SMs (4096 CTAs first block) and is correct in isolation (relerr 1e-7) but 14-26% SLOWER end-to-end / 2x slower in isolation, because the Wpart HBM round-trip + finish launch cost more than the already-fast (16.9%, 256-CTA) serial reduction saves. (2) FINER TILES sweep (BM_Y/BNc_Y/NW_Y/BM_A/BNc_A/NW_A): shipped tiles are optimal -- every variation within +0.7% (noise) or regresses, down to -14% at BMA16_BNCA16. ROOT CAUSE: the YT is already fast with 256 CTAs (>148 SMs); the apply is BANDWIDTH-bound (reads V/YT/A, writes A -- same read-A-twice C-floor as n512), not occupancy-starved (already 32768 CTAs). The real n=2048 headroom is the PANEL (53.4%, grid=8 CTAs, occupancy-starved) which needs MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX (split one matrix's row-reduction across SMs with cross-CTA/cluster comm), NOT a trailing reshape -- that is worker-1's angle. Comment-only record (split-YT reverted as both broken-on-integration AND slower); kernel byte-identical (benchmark 2167us vs NO_TRANS parent 2169us).

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- reshaping the n=2048 trailing to fill idle SMs is MEASURED-NEGATIVE, and I have the per-kernel breakdown that shows WHY (metric stays NO_TRANS parent 2167us, byte-identical commit 5ef6310a). KEY DATA -- torch-profiler per-kernel of n=2048 B=8 (total 8113us/iter): PANEL 4329us (53.4%, grid=8 CTAs serial), APPLY 2417us (29.8%, already 32768 CTAs), YT 1367us (16.9%, already 256 CTAs). The trailing is NOT the occupancy bottleneck -- the PANEL is. I tested BOTH brief levers: (1) ROW-SPLIT YT (grid (nct,nrt,B) one-dot/CTA + finishW sum -- I built it, wired it into the n=2048 path, validated correct in isolation at relerr 1e-7): it DOES fill the SMs (4096 CTAs first block) but is 14-26% SLOWER end-to-end / 2x slower isolated, because the Wpart HBM round-trip + finish launch cost more than the already-fast 256-CTA serial reduction saves; reverted. (2) FINER-TILE sweep of all 6 trailing tile knobs: shipped tiles are optimal (every variation +0.7% noise or worse, -14% at the finest). ROOT CAUSE: the YT already has 256 CTAs (>148 SMs) so splitting only adds HBM traffic; the apply is BANDWIDTH-bound (reads V/YT/A + writes A, the same read-A-twice floor I proved for n512), not occupancy-starved (32768 CTAs). The trailing is at its roofline. THE REAL n=2048 HEADROOM IS THE PANEL: 53.4%, grid=8 CTAs, occupancy-starved on 148 SMs. The Householder COLUMN chain is serial, but each column's REDUCTION over the up-to-2048 rows is parallel -- so the lever is MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX: assign several CTAs to each of the 8 matrices, split the per-column row-reduction across them, communicate the partial dots/norms via global atomics or sm_100 thread-block CLUSTERS (distributed shared memory). That fills the idle SMs AND shortens the per-column reduction latency. This is exactly worker-1's flagged angle and the ONE place with genuine roofline headroom at n=2048 -- I recommend pointing a panel-scoped brief (mine or worker-1's) at the multi-CTA-per-matrix panel reduction. I have no trailing hypotheses left; the n=2048 trailing, like n512, is saturated/bandwidth-bound.

n2048/n512 trailing are at roofline (you proved it); panel m-split is a confirmed dead end (W1/W3: per-reflector cross-CTA sync = TSQR barrier wall) and CholeskyQR for n2048 is W0's lane. Take a fresh SCORED lever nobody has hunted: W2 found a 215us DtoD memcpy (5.3%) at n512 in the graph-capture/routing path -- a real GPU-STREAM copy (scored, unlike host overhead). Profile the custom_kernel graph wrapper + _custom_kernel_impl routing on EVERY shape with nsys cuda_gpu_kern_sum, find all DtoD memcpys / .clone()/.contiguous()/output-pool copies that run ON the timed stream, and eliminate the avoidable ones (write kernels in-place to the output buffer, drop the residual clone, reuse the input buffer where the data_ptr-match invariant allows). Because the geomean weights all 12 shapes EQUALLY, shaving a per-call scored copy off each shape compounds. Extend graph zero-copy to count>1 shapes -> kill scored input-copy DtoD memcpys. The zero-copy path was capped at depth==1 (n512/n1024, count==1), leaving a SCORED DtoD static_in.copy_(data) on every count>1 shape. Measured per-shape input-copy DtoD (torch profiler): n176 3.1us, n352 6.8us, n2048 44us, n4096 88us (n512/n1024/n32 already 0 via zero-copy). The per-OBJECT binding (id(data)+weakref-is+data_ptr+sig check) is ALREADY safe for count>1 -- each persistent timed-loop tensor gets its own bound graph reading its own address; any fresh/one-shot caller (warmup/guards/tests) never matches a live binding -> copy-path -> safe. Raising QR_GRAPH_ZEROCOPY_MAXDEPTH 1->64 (== _GRAPH_ADDR_MAX cap) lets n176 (count 54), n352 (13), n2048 (2) bind per-object graphs -> input-copy DtoD -> 0 (measured); n4096's remaining 44us is the separate H=A.clone() inside _w2_qr_2level (not the input copy). diff_correctness_guard PASSES (the prior comment's 'diff guard hazard' was about data_ptr identity; this path keys on the tensor OBJECT which allocator reuse cannot alias), plus invariance + offgrid PASS. Because the geomean weights all 12 shapes equally, removing these scored copies compounds. Benchmark 2164.98us vs NO_TRANS parent 2168.74us (-0.17%, within noise but the copies are deterministically removed -> strictly less scored GPU work, cannot regress).
